This tutorial shows how to use a simple vaccination, that acts independently of any environmental intervention. 


## Products and interventions

In addition to direct modification of environmental shedding (previous tutorial), vaccination uses Starsim's _products_ and _deliveries_. A vaccine product, `ss.Vaccine(efficacy=...)`, which reduces susceptibility to infection, can be delivered with `ss.vaccinate()`:

- with no `interval` or `at`, as routine vaccination: each person is offered it once, when they first become eligible (e.g. `where=ss.ppl.age < 5`);
- with `at=[...]` or `interval=...`, in campaigns or rounds.

Typhoidsim also has `ty.vaccination_with_waning()`, a purpose-built implementation of typhoid vaccine schedules with boosters and optional age-specific waning, which returns the deliveries to pass to the sim.

The next tutorial will describe diagnostic and screening interventions.

```{python}
import starsim as ss
import typhoidsim as ty

# Define high-level simulation parameters
pars = dict(
    start    = 2000,          # Starting year
    dur      = ss.years(2),   # Duration of the simulation
    dt       = ss.weeks(1),   # Timestep of 1 week
    verbose  = 0,             # Do not print details of the run
)

def make_sim(interventions=None):
    """ Each sim needs its own people, network, and disease """
    ppl = ss.People(50_000) # The population
    random_p2p = ss.RandomNet(n_contacts=10) # Person to person transmission
    typhoid = ty.Typhoid(tppi=0.1, init_seroprev=0.8, init_prev=0.001) # The disease
    return ss.Sim(pars=pars, people=ppl, networks=random_p2p, diseases=typhoid, interventions=interventions)

# Create products
vax1 = ss.Vaccine(efficacy=0.4)
vax2 = ss.Vaccine(efficacy=0.8)

# Create the interventions
my_intervention_vax1 = ss.vaccinate(
    vax1,                # Use vax 1
    start=2000,          # Begin vaccination in 2000
    coverage=0.2,        # 20% coverage
)

my_intervention_vax2 = ss.vaccinate(
    vax2,                # Use vax 2
    start=2000,          # Begin vaccination in 2000
    coverage=0.2,        # 20% coverage
)

# Now create three sims: a baseline sim and one with each intervention
sim_base = make_sim().run()
sim_vax1 = make_sim(my_intervention_vax1).run()
sim_vax2 = make_sim(my_intervention_vax2).run()
```

```{python}
sim_base.plot()
```

```{python}
sim_vax1.plot()
```

```{python}
sim_vax2.plot()
```

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

res_base = sim_base.results
res_vax1 = sim_vax1.results
res_vax2 = sim_vax2.results

plt.figure()
plt.plot(res_base.timevec, res_base.typhoid.infections, label='Baseline')
plt.plot(res_vax1.timevec, res_vax1.typhoid.infections, label='Vax 1')
plt.plot(res_vax2.timevec, res_vax2.typhoid.infections, label='Vax 2')

plt.axvline(x=ss.date(2000), color='k', ls='--')
plt.title('New infections')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```
